key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni–20Cr+40TiC reduced oxidation weight gain by 95.71% relative to bare SA516 boiler steel, outperforming the other tested coatings.
engineering_relevance: This coating is a promising option for protecting SA516 boiler steel from high-temperature oxidation through a dense protective oxide layer.
method: Apply Ni–20Cr, Ni–20Cr+40TiC, and Ni–20Cr+40TiN coatings using HVOF and plasma spraying.
Characterize microstructure and phases using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: Laboratory testing showed severe oxide spalling and cracking on bare steel, while the best coating reduced weight gain by 95.71%; improved protection was attributed to Cr₂O₃, TiO₂, NiTiO₄, and NiO formation.
watch_item: Performance over 50 laboratory air-oxidation cycles does not establish long-term durability in corrosive boiler service.
paper_title: Microstructure and high-temperature oxidation behaviour of HVOF and plasma sprayed Ni–Cr-based ceramic coatings on SA516 boiler steel
